moveDecisions.rationale: The categorical-reasons thesis and its desire-independent contrast remain recoverable and stable, while a bounded qualification is left implicit.

The move directly replaces explanationist necessity with defeasible appearance justification and addresses both initial support and the role of specific defeaters.

The move supplies contrary motivational material without answering alienation itself, while clearly and cautiously representing how moral belief can organize existing desires.

The move fully explains the causal-model alternative, centrally supports explanationist evidence, and presents a clear probability-level claim with only an implicit qualification.

The move fairly answers the narrow synonym test by presenting the strongest broader analytic interpretation and accurately locating the role of phenomenal concept mastery.
The move contacts all three live targets through its objective-natures account, while its unqualified language asserts a strong probability beyond the compressed warrant.
